body:
This branch of the `if constexpr` is the one CI actually runs. The shared window, the unit cut, the VNNI block store and all of `check_window` above only execute with `TRON_K_VNNI=ON`, and nothing PR-gated builds that way: the option defaults OFF, the required Nix test build sets no flag, and the only ON lane is the legacy workflow, which fires on manual dispatch or publish-deb's nightly and tag triggers and has zero runs on this branch. AGENTS.md wants every committed test to run in CI unless the user explicitly approves an exception, and #4865 has no comment recording one.

Could we add an option-on variant of the required Nix test build that runs `t_llama_unit "[k_vnni]"` and `t_k_vnni_layout`? If an exception is the intent instead, I think it needs to be on record on #4865 before this merges.

Checked by: `grep -n TRON_K_VNNI CMakeLists.txt nix/*.nix .github/workflows/*.yml` plus the workflow triggers and `gh run list --workflow=cmake-single-platform.yml --branch jhan-vnnik-3-shared-save` -> option OFF by default, ON only in the legacy workflow, `[]` runs on this branch.

On the unshared path this now stores every K row of the minibatch before the first `mark_k_complete` or GOF credit. The parent interleaved store, mark and credit per token, and in the handwritten llama plugin the K and V callbacks are independent, so V can land first and a layer's first GOF now waits for the whole K store instead of its first four tokens.

Could we either call `store_k_block` per unit of the cut here and mark that unit's tokens after each store, or add a sentence to the Note saying the unshared path now marks after the whole store and why that delay is accepted?

Checked by: `git diff --merge-base origin/jhan-vnnik-2-amx HEAD -- h/tron/models/model.hpp` with `sed -n 972,1002p h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp` and `grep -n "gof_tokens =" h/tron/gof.hpp` -> the per-token loop lost its store, `launch_wk` and `launch_wv` are separate callbacks, a GOF is 4 tokens.

This wait has no watchdog, and windows pair by call count rather than by which operation opened them. Today both sides are emitted from the same statement list with the same `n_workers`, so the counts can't drift, but if they ever did a helper would pair with the wrong window and spin here forever with no diagnostic.

Two cheap guards: mirror main's clock check in this loop, and stamp the window with the slot id and `n_workers` before the release so each worker can assert them after the acquire.

Checked by: `sed -n 3335,3338p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `grep -n '"n_workers"' ingest/src/TronCpp.hs` -> a bare `_mm_pause` loop with no clock read; both sides get the same `n_workers` from the generator.

+    // Note [Shared block save]

+    // save_k stores the K rows of every token of the minibatch once per

+    // measurement of 2026-09-14 on the test server delphi-3bda (model
+    // qwen3-4b, 8 users, prompt 1024, 128 tokens of each user per pass) gave
+    // 0.86 ms per layer, 105 ns per (token, KV head) row for that per-token
+    // store. The attention workers' pending sections wait behind it. Two
+    // things shorten it:
+    //   1. Block save (store_block in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp, page::set_k_block):
+    //      a run of the pass's tokens that fills (part of) one 16-token block of
+    //      a page is transposed in registers. It is then written as whole 64-byte
+    //      lines, instead of one 4-byte scatter per (token, dimension pair, line).
+    //      Chosen per run in store_k_block.
+    //   2. Sharing with the main helpers: in generated plugins the helpers
+    //      are idle while main runs save_k. Their next kernel waits for the
+    //      attention output. So the generated run_main_help calls save_k at
+    //      the same statement position, with the helper's worker_ix. One
+    //      function serves both sides: worker_ix 0 is main, 1 .. n_workers - 1
+    //      are the helpers. Every thread then claims work units (runs of
+    //      consecutive items inside one 16-token block, see the protocol
+    //      below) until none is left. n_workers == 1 never shares (the
+    //      handwritten plugins, and the unit tests except the shared-save case
+    //      of t_llama_unit).
+    // The window protocol (fields in batch::k_store_window, common.hpp):
+    //   - both sides decide with k_store_shared(). A window exists only
+    //     when it says yes. So a helper never waits for a window main does
+    //     not open. (A pass with at most 16 items, such as a decode step, or
+    //     more than 128 workers is not shared.)
+    //   - main cuts the item list into work units (unit_start[]). A unit is a
+    //     run of consecutive items in one 16-token block of one page with the
+    //     same token_jobs_do_kv value. Items of one block that are not
+    //     consecutive fall into several units. Their writers use masked
+    //     stores on disjoint token lanes. So two threads may write one block
+    //     without conflict. When a run fills the block, the block gets one
+    //     full-line store per pair row. Main then zeroes the claim counter
+    //     and `finished`. Next it increments `opened` (release). A helper's
+    //     W-th call waits for `opened` >= W
+    //     (acquire). So window W of a pass is the W-th shared save_k of that
+    //     pass on both sides.
+    //   - every thread claims units with fetch_add on `next_unit`. It stores
+    //     the rows of each unit it claims. A unit index is assigned once. So
+    //     a thread that leaves the claim loop has stored every unit it took.
+    //   - a helper increments `finished` (release) when its claim loop ends.
+    //     Main returns only when `finished` == n_workers - 1 (acquire). Four
+    //     things follow once main returns. Every unit is stored. No helper is
+    //     inside a window main has left. The counters are main's to reset.
+    //     Every row store happens-before the downstream latch count_down
+    //     below.
+    //   - the per-token completion marks and GOF credits stay on main, after
+    //     the join, in q_batch->items order, one token at a time.
+    // The rows a helper reads (ks) are ready for two reasons. Main waited for
+    // every token's K channel before calling save_k (the generated code). The
+    // channel phase cannot advance while main is inside save_k. A helper can
+    // reach its save_k call without main's help. Nothing blocks between its
+    // K/Q rope kernel and this statement. So main's join cannot deadlock. A
+    // join that does not complete within about two minutes
+    // (k_join_timeout_s after the first clock read) aborts with the
+    // counters in the message.
+
+    // Tokens per page block: the size of one block save and the longest run.
+    static constexpr size_t k_store_block = k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16;
+    // A run of this length is stored row by row (set_k_row), not as a block.
+    static constexpr size_t k_scatter_run_len = 1;
body:
With this at 1, every run of two or more tokens takes the block store, whose cost is roughly flat in run length, so short runs store slower than the per-token scatters would. On the AMD host I measured, the crossover is 5 to 6 tokens hot and 12 to 13 cold. Granite Rapids is the target, so the number there may differ.

Could we measure n = 1..16 on Granite Rapids, set this constant from that crossover, and write the compare at line 3260 as `if (n <= k_scatter_run_len)` so the constant reads as "up to this length scatters"?

Checked by: `/tmp/pr4958-probes/crossover.cpp` (store_row, store_block and the transpose replicated verbatim, `clang++ -O2 -mavx512f -mavx512bw -mavx512dq -mavx512vl`) on AMD EPYC 9654 -> hot `n=2 scatter 58.9 ns / block 145.9 ns`, `n=5 143.0 / 146.0`, `n=6 169.7 / 146.5`; cold `n=12 461.3 / 467.6`, `n=13 511.8 / 474.7`.

This and the join at line 3354 are the only raw `_mm_pause` spins in the C++ tree. The main/helper barrier this batch already uses waits through the mwaitx readiness source, which halts the core and has a timed overload.

Could we widen `opened` and `finished` to `std::atomic_uint64_t` and wait with `readiness_source::atomic(&w.opened).wait_geq(my_window)`, with the timed overload for the join? That would also replace the hand-rolled clock loop below.

Checked by: `grep -rn "_mm_pause" --include=*.cpp --include=*.hpp h src` and `grep -n "void wait_geq(" h/system/mwaitx.hpp` -> pause spins only at model.hpp:3337 and :3354; `wait_geq(uint64_t val, uint64_t wait_ns = timeout_never)` at mwaitx.hpp:228.

The concurrency checks in this section all run after the helpers are joined. So whether a helper arrives before the open is a thread-start race the test doesn't control, nothing asserts that a helper actually stored a unit, and by the same control flow a `finished` increment placed before the stores would pass.

Three small additions would pin it: an ordering where main sleeps before its call for window two so the helpers must wait on `opened`, recording the claiming worker per unit and requiring that a helper claimed at least one, and gating one helper mid-store to check main can't return early.

Checked by: `sed -n 4052,4066p t/t_llama_unit.cpp` and `sed -n 4076,4132p t/t_llama_unit.cpp` -> every assertion runs after both joins and none names the claiming worker; the early-`finished` mutant is inferred from the control flow, not run.

The sharing gate's boundaries have no test: the only multi-worker call is 48 items with 3 workers, no helper ever calls `save_k` on a pass of at most 16 items, and nothing uses a worker index of 128 or above. Those are the "helper returns without waiting" edges, which are the ones that hang if the gate ever disagrees between sides.

Could we add a 16-item, 3-worker section asserting `opened == 0` and every row stored once, and one call with `worker_ix = 128, n_workers = 129` asserting the same?

Checked by: `grep -rn "save_k<" t/` and `grep -n "max_shared_workers\|129" t/t_llama_unit.cpp` -> the only worker-index calls are at t_llama_unit.cpp:4056-4061 with `n_workers = 3` on 48 items; no hits for the bound.

This in-place bf16 branch, the one every production executor takes, isn't covered by the unit test: the test's executor gives the K buffer a float scalar, so only the conversion branch below runs.

Could we instantiate the save_k case over `host_bf16` as well, reusing the same snapshot and check lambdas?

Checked by: `/tmp/pr4958-probes/kv_elem.cpp` replicating the `kv_elem_t` derivation, `clang++-19 ... -fsyntax-only` under the test TU's recorded flags -> `static_assert` that the test executor yields `float` and `host_bf16` yields `bf16` passes; flipping the first to `bf16` fails.

A decode step with 17 or more users satisfies `k_store_shared` and opens a window per layer, but the PR measured decode only at 8 users, and this parenthetical reads as though decode never shares.

Could we measure decode at 32 users against head, or raise the threshold, and reword this to "a decode step with at most 16 users"?

Checked by: `sed -n 3157,3159p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `gh pr view 4958 --json body --jq .body | sed -n '78p;87p'` -> the gate is `n_workers > 1 && ... && items.size() > 16`; the PR's decode run is `qwen3-4b, 8 users`.

body:
The grouping rule now lives in two places and they disagree: this cutter ends a unit when the KV flag flips, while the run loop in `store_k_block` (line 3248) skips KV-less jobs without ending a run. So a block with a hole stores as one masked block when unshared and as two partial blocks plus an idle unit when shared.

Could the cutter skip KV-less items and open a unit only on a page or block change of KV items, so the cut is the single grouping? The test loops at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:4112 and 4127 would relax accordingly.

Checked by: `sed -n 3182p h/tron/models/model.hpp`, `sed -n 3248p h/tron/models/model.hpp`, `sed -n 3367p h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> `kv != run_kv` ends a unit here; `continue` with no `break` in the run loop; the unshared path runs that loop over the whole batch.

A repeated page offset inside a run is unreachable (the scheduler keeps one job per token), so I'd rather this abort than quietly start a second run. A silent `break` here would hide a scheduler bug as a slower store.

```suggestion
            TRON_ASSERT(!(present & bit),
                "save_k: page offset {} appears twice in one run", j);
```

Checked by: `sed -n 1877p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 2457,2458p h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp` -> one job per token, and the scheduler piggybacks a listener rather than adding a second KV job.

Not about this line, just the nearest place to put it: #4958 is marked ready while its base #4957 is open, and #4957 is ready on #4956. AGENTS.md's stack rule says only the PR based on `main` may be ready for review; the others stay draft until their parent merges. The body already says "draft until PR #4957 merges", so I think it's just the flag.

Could we `gh pr ready --undo 4958 && gh pr ready --undo 4957` for now?

Checked by: `gh pr view <n> --json isDraft,baseRefName,state` for 4956, 4957, 4958 -> all three `isDraft: false`, OPEN, on bases `main`, `jhan-vnnik-1-layout`, `jhan-vnnik-2-amx`.

This test and `t_llama_unit` both changed materially, and t/AGENTS.md asks for a `config/test-benchmarks.json` refresh after that. The diff touches nothing under config/, and the body defers the refresh to #4959.

Could we run `bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit t_k_vnni_layout` from the route's Slice name and commit the rows here, so the Granite Rapids runtime of this case lands with the change that created it?

Checked by: `sed -n 23,25p t/AGENTS.md` and `git diff --merge-base origin/jhan-vnnik-2-amx HEAD --stat` -> the refresh rule; nine changed files, none under `config/`.

The first commit (c47be18df8) references Note [Shared block save] here and in two other files, but the Note itself only arrives in bb342d9033, so that interior commit fails `make lint-notes`. The head passes. A bisect landing on the first commit would hit the lint.

Could we either move the Note's definition into c47be18df8, or drop the three references there and add them with the Note?

Checked by: `git archive c47be18df8 | tar -x -C /tmp/c47 && make -C /tmp/c47 lint-notes` -> `h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:689:9: error: Reference to undefined Note [Shared block save]` (and the two others), `Error 1`; `make lint-notes` at HEAD -> exit 0.

These checks count `save_k` calls and search both argument texts over the whole translation unit. So a generator that swapped the two argument lists between `run()` and `run_main_help()` would still pass, and the helper call's position inside `run_main_help` is never asserted. Same for the shared-module case at line 3575.

Could we extract the `run(` and `run_main_help(` method bodies and assert the ordered projection of the `save_k` call in each?

Checked by: `sed -n 3153,3162p ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs` and `sed -n 3575,3578p ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs` -> `Txt.count` over `cpp` and two `Txt.isInfixOf` checks over `compactCpp cpp`, no slicing by method in either hunk.

This cut is recomputed on main's critical path for every shared window of every layer, but its inputs (`items`, `token_jobs`, `token_jobs_do_kv`) are assigned once per forward, so the result is identical for every window of the pass.

Could we cut once per batch per forward, behind a `bool units_cut` in `k_store_window_t` that construct_minibatches clears?

Checked by: `grep -n "k_store_cut_units(q_batch)" h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 1751,1752p h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> the call sits inside the per-call shared branch; `token_jobs = in_token_jobs; token_jobs_do_kv = in_token_jobs_do_kv;` happens once in `forward`.

Every unit costs one contended `fetch_add` here, and in a decode minibatch every item is one token on its own page, so every unit is a single token.

Could we claim units in chunks, something like `max(1, n_units / (4 * n_workers))`, so the counter is touched a handful of times per worker instead of once per token?

Checked by: `sed -n 3342p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 3182p h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> `fetch_add(1, ...)` inside the per-unit loop; `pg != run_page` opens a new unit on every page change.

body:
The deadlock argument here ("Nothing blocks between its K/Q rope kernel and this statement") rests on the shape of today's emitted schedule, which the generator can change without touching this file. TronCpp.hs already states the rule the argument needs: deadlock freedom follows from ordering, and attention workers make their lane-side calls in main's order.

Could we rewrite these three sentences to cite that ordering rule instead of the current schedule?

Checked by: `sed -n 3132,3134p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 1845,1848p ingest/src/TronCpp.hs` -> the schedule-shaped sentence here; `Deadlock freedom follows from ordering and needs no separate check` in the generator.

body:
"The counters are main's to reset" is only half true: `next_unit` and `finished` are reset per window, while `opened` and `helper_windows` are never written back to zero and pair over the batch's one-forward lifetime. That's load-bearing for the pairing, so I'd say it outright, something like: "Main resets `next_unit` and `finished` per window; `opened` and `helper_windows` are monotone for the batch's lifetime, which is one forward." The field comment in common.hpp ("Windows opened so far in this pass") could say the same.

Checked by: `grep -n "store(0\|opened\.\|helper_windows\[" h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> stores to `next_unit` and `finished` at 3331-3332; only `fetch_add` and `++` on `opened` and `helper_windows`.

body:
`store_block` takes an intrinsic mask plus an unbounded array of nullable row pointers, and a present bit with a null row dereferences null right here. No caller in this PR does that, but the signature allows it.

Could we assert it before the load, or derive `present` from the non-null entries of a `std::span<const bf16* const, 16>` so the two can't disagree?

```cpp
TRON_ASSERT(!((present >> t) & 1u) || rows[t] != nullptr,
    "store_block: present token {} has no row", t);
```

Checked by: `/tmp/pr4958-probes/nullrow.cpp` (the same load loop with `present = 1`, `rows[0] = nullptr`) -> `Segmentation fault`, exit 139.

This pins the claim loop's implementation rather than its contract: a compare-exchange claim loop that stops at `n_units` would be correct and fail here. I see the comment above wants to catch a helper that skipped its claim loop; recording the claiming worker per unit (as in my comment on the thread spawn above) covers that directly, and this can then check the contract.

```suggestion
      REQUIRE(w.next_unit.load() >= w.n_units);
```

Checked by: `sed -n 4096p t/t_llama_unit.cpp` -> `REQUIRE(w.next_unit.load() == w.n_units + n_workers);`.

`checked` restates the loop bounds, so this REQUIRE can't fail; the memcmp inside the loop is the real assertion. Could we drop the counter and this line? (The `n_units >= 1` in t_llama_unit is a different case: weak, but a live production invariant.)

Checked by: `sed -n 229,246p t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp` -> `++checked` once per iteration of the two loops whose bounds the REQUIRE restates.

120 s is about five orders of magnitude above a prefill layer's K store (the Note's own figure is 0.86 ms unshared), so a hung join alarms two minutes into a stalled prefill. I know the body flags this one for reviewers; my vote is 10 s, still absurdly generous for a store and short enough that a serving stall gets its diagnostic quickly. The "about two minutes" at line 3134 would follow.

```suggestion
    static constexpr int k_join_timeout_s = 10;
```

Checked by: `sed -n 3148p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 3084p h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> `k_join_timeout_s = 120` against `0.86 ms per layer`.

+    //   - main cuts the item list into work units (unit_start[]). A unit is a
+    //     run of consecutive items in one 16-token block of one page with the
+    //     same token_jobs_do_kv value. Items of one block that are not
+    //     consecutive fall into several units. Their writers use masked
+    //     stores on disjoint token lanes. So two threads may write one block
+    //     without conflict. When a run fills the block, the block gets one
+    //     full-line store per pair row. Main then zeroes the claim counter
+    //     and `finished`. Next it increments `opened` (release). A helper's
+    //     W-th call waits for `opened` >= W
+    //     (acquire). So window W of a pass is the W-th shared save_k of that
+    //     pass on both sides.
+    //   - every thread claims units with fetch_add on `next_unit`. It stores
+    //     the rows of each unit it claims. A unit index is assigned once. So
+    //     a thread that leaves the claim loop has stored every unit it took.
+    //   - a helper increments `finished` (release) when its claim loop ends.
+    //     Main returns only when `finished` == n_workers - 1 (acquire). Four
+    //     things follow once main returns. Every unit is stored. No helper is
+    //     inside a window main has left. The counters are main's to reset.
+    //     Every row store happens-before the downstream latch count_down
+    //     below.
+    //   - the per-token completion marks and GOF credits stay on main, after
+    //     the join, in q_batch->items order, one token at a time.
+    // The rows a helper reads (ks) are ready for two reasons. Main waited for
+    // every token's K channel before calling save_k (the generated code). The
+    // channel phase cannot advance while main is inside save_k. A helper can
+    // reach its save_k call without main's help. Nothing blocks between its
+    // K/Q rope kernel and this statement. So main's join cannot deadlock. A
+    // join that does not complete within about two minutes
+    // (k_join_timeout_s after the first clock read) aborts with the
+    // counters in the message.
+
+    // Tokens per page block: the size of one block save and the longest run.
+    static constexpr size_t k_store_block = k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16;
+    // A run of this length is stored row by row (set_k_row), not as a block.
+    static constexpr size_t k_scatter_run_len = 1;
+    // The join watchdog of Note [Shared block save]: main reads the clock once
+    // every k_join_clock_spins pause loops. It aborts k_join_timeout_s seconds
+    // after the first clock read.
+    static constexpr uint64_t k_join_clock_spins = 1048576;  // 2^20
+    static_assert((k_join_clock_spins & (k_join_clock_spins - 1)) == 0,
+        "the spin count is a power of two: the check below masks with it");
+    static constexpr int k_join_timeout_s = 120;
+
+    // Whether the K store of this minibatch is shared with the helpers. The
+    // answer is the same on the main thread and on every helper.
+    template <attention_geometry geometry>
+    bool k_store_shared(batch* q_batch, size_t n_workers) const noexcept {
+      if constexpr (!k_vnni::layout_on<geometry.kv.head_size>) {
+        return false;
+      } else {
+        return n_workers > 1 &&
+               n_workers <= q_batch->k_store_window.helper_windows.size() &&
+               q_batch->items.size() > k_store_block;
+      }
+    }
+
+    // Cut the minibatch's items into the work units of Note [Shared block save].
+    // Only main calls this, before it opens the window.
+    void k_store_cut_units(batch* q_batch) noexcept {
+      auto& w = q_batch->k_store_window;
+      auto const& self = *this;
+      const size_t n_items = q_batch->items.size();
+      TRON_ASSERT(n_items + 1 <= w.unit_start.size(),
+          "save_k: {} items exceed the K store window's unit table", n_items);
+      uint32_t n_units = 0;
+      const page* run_page = nullptr;
+      size_t run_block = 0;
+      bool run_kv = false;
+      for (size_t t = 0; t < n_items; ++t) {
+        const token_job_id ix = q_batch->items[t];
+        const bool kv = self.token_jobs_do_kv[ix] != 0;
+        const page* pg = kv ? &page_of(token_jobs[ix]) : nullptr;
+        const size_t block =
+            kv ? static_cast<size_t>(pg->offset_in_page(token_jobs[ix])) / k_store_block
+               : 0;
+        if (t == 0 || kv != run_kv || pg != run_page || block != run_block) {
+          w.unit_start[n_units++] = static_cast<uint32_t>(t);
+          run_kv = kv;
+          run_page = pg;
+          run_block = block;
+        }
+      }
+      w.unit_start[n_units] = static_cast<uint32_t>(n_items);
+      w.n_units = n_units;
+    }
+
+    // Store the K rows (every KV head) of the tokens items[task_begin,
+    // task_end) of q_batch into slot `slot`. VNNI slots: consecutive items
+    // that fall into the same 16-token block of the same page are stored as
+    // one block (set_k_block). A run of one token is stored with set_k_row
+    // (scatter). Row-major slots: one row store per token and KV head

+    // does them after every store is done.

`store_k_block` stores an item range and picks among three mechanisms, while `k_vnni::store_block` stores exactly one block, so the two names read as the same thing at different layers. Could we rename this one to `store_k_range`? The Note already keeps "run" and "block" apart for the same reason.

Checked by: `sed -n 3201,3206p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 342,345p h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp` -> `store_k_block(batch*, kv_slot_id, kv_buffer_t&, size_t task_begin, size_t task_end)` against `store_block(k_vnni_view, size_t c, __mmask16 present, const bf16* const rows[16])`.

A default-constructed time point is standing in for "clock not yet read" here and at line 3357. Could we make the absence explicit with `std::optional<std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point> t0;` and `if (!t0) t0 = now;`, or just read the clock once before the loop? The second is simpler and costs one clock read per shared window.

Checked by: `sed -n 3352p h/tron/models/model.hpp` and `sed -n 3357p h/tron/models/model.hpp` -> `time_point t0{};` and `if (t0 == std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{}) t0 = now;`.

The `[[maybe_unused]]` isn't needed: this is a plain `TEST_CASE`, not a template, so the lambda is odr-used by the discarded `if constexpr` branch and no compiler warns. I compiled the pattern under clang 19 (the CI compiler) and three others with the project's warning flags, with and without the attribute, and got zero warnings every way. Could we drop it and let clang-format re-align the second parameter?

Checked by: `/tmp/pr4958-probes/mu.cpp` compiled with `-Wall -Wpedantic -Wextra -Wno-shadow` under clang 19.1.7, GCC 15.3.0, GCC 11.4 and clang 14, `LAYOUT_ON` 0 and 1 -> 0 warnings in every configuration.
